findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_registry" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Returns the full attribute registry — every searchable and filterable field, its type, allowed values, and display label. Read this first to understand the sche…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_listings, get_listing, look_up_parcel, get_parcel, save_search · Private data: get_listing, look_up_parcel, get_parcel · Public sink: interpret_search, look_up_parcel, save_search, update_listing, set_listing_attributes, attach_listing_photo · Destructive: delete_saved_search.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_listings, get_listing, look_up_parcel, get_parcel, save_search · Private data: get_listing, look_up_parcel, get_parcel · Public sink: interpret_search, look_up_parcel, save_search, update_listing, set_listing_attributes, attach_listing_photo · Destructive: delete_saved_search

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_listing" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
